data.cultural_impact: The term "Sunan" in Islamic culture refers to the established customs, manners, and traditions of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his companions. These Sunan serve as a model for Muslims to follow in their daily lives, reflecting the moral and ethical values of Islam. They cover various aspects of life, from prayer and fasting to personal conduct and social interactions. By adhering to these Sunan, Muslims strive to create a harmonious and orderly community in line with Islamic teachings.
data.spiritual_significance: The practice of Sunan holds deep spiritual significance for Muslims as it serves as a means to draw closer to Allah (SWT) and emulate His Messenger (PBUH). By adhering to these Sunan, Muslims seek to please Allah and make their actions consistent with His guidance. Moreover, the performance of Sunan fosters a sense of peace, tranquility, and inner calm, as one harmonizes their actions with the teachings and practices of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The pursuit of Sunan, therefore, is a cornerstone of many Muslims' spiritual journeys and a sacred commitment that aids them in their quest for closeness to Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, in his work 'Al-Isaba fi Tamyiz as-Sahaba', records that Sunan Abu Dawood was born in the year 819 AD (202 AH) in Ash-Sham (Syria). The name 'Sunan' means 'ways' or 'paths' in Arabic, and is believed to have been given to Abu Dawood due to his extensive collection of Hadiths, which provide the 'paths' to understanding Islamic law and practice.
historical_references.context: Birth and origin of the name 'Sunan' for Abu Dawood

historical_references.reference: Al-Dhahabi, in his work 'Siyar A'lam an-Nubala', states that Sunan Abu Dawood died in the year 888 AD (252 AH) in Bukhara (Central Asia). The collection of Hadiths that bears his name, 'Sunan Abu Dawood', is considered one of the six authentic collections of Hadith in Sunni Islam.
historical_references.context: Death and significance of Sunan Abu Dawood's collection of Hadiths
